en.title: fl
en.summary: This is the letter L338 from the alphabet vowel-consonant groups.

sections.title: The sound of fl
paragraphs: The letters fl make one smooth consonant blend. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. You hear this sound at the start of (flag) /flæɡ/, which means a piece of cloth with colours. The letters fl make one sound in English words.

sections.title: How to say fl
paragraphs: Place your upper teeth gently on your lower lip. Blow air through the narrow gap without voice. Quickly touch your tongue tip to the ridge behind your upper teeth. Let the air pass along the sides of your tongue. Touch your throat to feel your voice turn on as you say the second part.

sections.title: Spelling of fl
paragraphs: The letters fl appear at the start and in the middle of words. They always make the same blended sound. You hear this clear sound in (flat) /flæt/. It also appears across syllables inside words, keeping both consonants joined smoothly.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not insert an extra vowel between the two consonants. Many learners say an extra beat, turning one syllable into two. Keep the transition completely smooth, gliding straight from the teeth to the tongue ridge. There is no other pitfall with this letter pair.
